newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks plunge again on rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks plunge again on rate worries.

text.p: Jakarta stocks were pounded again on Monday as investors sold down their holdings on worries over higher interest rates and sharp declines in neighbouring markets, brokers said.
"Worries over high interest rates and the sharp falls in Malaysia and the Philippines prompted players, particularly foreigners, to step up their selling," one broker said.

The Jakarta composite index fell 17.27 points, or 2.56 percent, to close at 658.17 points. Last week the index fell 6.4 percent as the central bank's moves to restrict liquidity following speculative attacks on the rupiah led to a spike in interest rates.

Brokers and analysts said fresh weakness in the Malaysian ringgit and the Philippine peso, and a spillover onto the rupiah, haunted the Jakarta market on Monday and prompted a further sell-off on the local market.
"Players, particularly the foreigners, perceive Indonesia, neighbouring Malaysia, the Philippines and Thailand as having many similarities," one analyst said.
The analyst said players were worried the economic downturn in Thailand could also take place in other countries in the region.

Goei Siauw Hong, an analyst with Socgen Croby Securities, said Monday's sell-off was driven not just by concerns over higher domestic interest rates, but also by a fundamental change in perception over the risks of investing in the region.
"It is a change in perception as the region is now considered to be riskier than before and players are trying to reduce exposure in the region," Hong said.
Analysts said reports that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Asian nations led by Japan had pledged a total of $16 billion in loans to help the Thai economy failed to bolster sentiment.
Analysts said worries over expected slow foreign participation in the region and earnings disappointments due to the high interest rates had prompted the fresh sell-off.
"We expect the index to fall to around 630 levels at year-end, with likely disappointments over third quarter earnings due to the current high interest rates," Hong said.
"I heard the index could touch around 650 levels in the near term," an analyst with Nomura Indonesia brokerage said earlier.
